events.text: On a slow ferry across the river, {npc} is the only other passenger, and has brought far too many dumplings.

effects.log: By the far bank you have traded life stories and addresses.
{npc} laughs at your technique the whole way. You arrive soaked and friends.

mem.note: rowed the ferry badly with me

events.text: {npc} is searching the whole town for a lost dog with one ear.

effects.log: You find it asleep in a noodle shop. {npc} hugs the dog, then you.
{npc} nods and keeps searching. You hear later the dog came home on its own.

events.text: In the teahouse, {npc} has been losing at xiangqi to the same old man for an hour and asks you to help.

ok.log: You win in eleven moves. The old man demands a rematch. {npc} buys you both tea.

mem.note: beat the old man at xiangqi for me

fail.log: You lose even faster. {npc} laughs so hard the old man joins in.

effects.log: The heckling becomes a friendship. The old man never forgives either of you.

events.text: A storm has torn the roof off {npc}'s shed and {he} is up there alone in the wind.

effects.log: Two hours, a hundred tiles, one near fall. You finish at dawn, laughing, soaked.

mem.note: fixed my roof in the storm

effects.log: It is not heroic, but {npc} does not fall. {He} remembers that.

events.text: A pickpocket grabs {npc}'s purse in the market and runs straight toward you.

ok.log: The thief goes flying. {npc} gets the purse back and insists on buying you lunch.

mem.note: caught the thief who robbed me

fail.log: He dodges you. You chase him three streets and lose him. {npc} still thanks you.

effects.log: The guards arrive late, as always. {npc} sighs. At least you tried.

events.text: {npc} is selling calligraphy by the road. It is very bad calligraphy.

effects.log: 'Nobody has ever bought one,' {npc} admits. You hang it on your wall. It is still bad. You like it.

ok.log: {npc} practises your way for a month and comes to show you. It is much better. You are friends now.

mem.note: taught me to hold a brush

fail.log: {npc} is offended, then curious, then asks for more advice.

events.text: {npc}'s horse has gone lame on the mountain road, miles from anywhere.

choices.text: Walk with {him} to the next town

effects.log: A long, slow walk. By the end you know about {his} whole family.

choices.text: Share your remedy for the leg

effects.log: The horse limps less. {npc} writes your name down 'so I remember who to thank'.

events.text: You and {npc} are both hired to guard a warehouse through a long, boring night.

effects.log: Nothing happens to the warehouse. Everything happens to the friendship.

mem.note: kept me awake with stories on night watch

effects.log: {npc} keeps watch while you sleep, and wakes you with hot tea. You owe {him} one.

events.text: At a wedding you barely wanted to attend, you are seated next to {npc}, who also barely wanted to attend.

effects.log: Quietly, behind your sleeves. It is the best wedding either of you has been to.
Neither of you can dance. Everyone remembers it.

events.text: In the public bathhouse, {npc} is arguing loudly with the attendant about the water temperature.

effects.log: Together you win: hotter water for everyone. {npc} treats you like a war comrade.

mem.note: stood with me in the bathhouse war

effects.log: You make peace. {npc} grumbles, then thanks you.

events.text: {npc} is trying to teach a crowd of village children to read, and losing.

effects.log: Two teachers, twenty children, one survives. Barely. You meet every week after that.
The children go silent. {npc} stares at you as if you were a miracle.

events.text: You and {npc} reach for the same rare herb on a cliff ledge at the same time.

effects.log: {npc} looks surprised, then splits it with you anyway.

ok.log: You get it. {npc} laughs: 'Next one is mine.' You go herb-hunting together after that.

fail.log: {npc} gets it, then offers you half. You feel ashamed and grateful.

events.text: {npc} reads a poem aloud in the teahouse. It is terrible. {He} looks straight at you.

effects.log: The room follows your lead. {npc} glows. You will hear many more poems.
{npc} is quiet, then laughs. 'Finally, an honest person.' {He} buys you tea every week.

mem.note: told me the truth about my poem

events.text: {npc} is cooking for a whole inn full of hungry travellers because the cook ran off.

effects.log: You chop until your arms hurt. At midnight the two of you eat the leftovers, exhausted and happy.
{npc} watches you eat every bite and asks your opinion on each dish.

events.text: {npc} is mending your old clothes by the lamp, the way {he} did when you were small.

effects.log: You talk about nothing much. It is one of the best evenings of the year.

mem.note: kept me company while I mended

effects.log: {npc} teaches you, very slowly, very patiently. Your stitches are awful.

mem.note: let me teach them to sew

events.text: {npc} finds your first tiny shoes in a chest and cannot stop laughing about how small your feet were.

effects.log: The whole house hears you. Nobody asks why.

mem.note: laughed with me over old things

effects.log: {npc} tells stories for hours. Half of them you do not remember. All of them are embarrassing.

variants: In the bottom of a chest, {npc} finds the tiny shoes you wore as a baby, and laughs until {he} has to sit down.

events.text: {npc} asks you to come along to the market to carry things, the way you used to.

effects.log: {npc} haggles like a general. You carry like a mule. It is a good day.
{npc} scolds you all the way home for wasting money, smiling the whole time.

variants: {npc} wants company at the market, and someone to carry the baskets, just like the old days.

events.text: You cannot sleep. Neither can {npc}. You end up in the kitchen at midnight.

effects.log: You say things you never have. {npc} says things back.
Nothing needs saying. The tea is good.

variants: Sleep will not come. You go to the kitchen for water and find {npc} already there in the dark, also awake.

events.text: The family house needs repairs, and {npc} is too proud to ask for help.

effects.log: You fix the gate, the roof and the well. {npc} pretends not to notice, then cooks your favourite dish.
'I can manage,' {npc} says. Then: 'The roof, maybe.'

variants: The family house is leaking and sagging, and {npc} would rather fix it alone than ask anyone.

events.text: {npc} wakes you in the middle of the night to show you the moon. It is very big and very orange.

effects.log: You watch until it sets. Neither of you says anything, and it is perfect.
You grumble. Then you watch. Then you stop grumbling.

events.text: {npc} has tried to cook your favourite dish as a surprise. It is on fire.

effects.log: It is terrible. You eat every bite. {npc} knows exactly what that means.
The second try is almost edible. The kitchen is ruined. You both laugh until you cry.

events.text: {npc} asks you to teach {him} one sword form, just one, just for fun.

effects.log: {npc} is terrible, then less terrible. By the end of the summer {he} can do it beautifully.
It stops being a sword form almost at once. Nobody minds.

mem.note: danced with me in the yard

events.text: {npc} wants to court the magistrate's daughter and begs you to deliver a poem, because {he} is too nervous.

effects.log: The daughter reads it, blushes and asks who wrote it. {npc} owes you forever.
{npc} goes. It goes terribly, then wonderfully. {He} thanks you anyway.

events.text: A rival dojo has challenged {npc}'s little school, and {he} has no fighters good enough.

ok.log: You win the challenge. The school is saved and {npc} puts your name on the wall.

fail.log: You lose, honourably. The school survives on stubbornness alone. {npc} does not blame you.

effects.log: {npc} nods stiffly. The school closes a year later.

mem.note: would not fight for my school

events.text: {npc} is moving to a new town and has far too many heavy chests.

effects.log: Three days, one cart, one bad back. {npc} gives you the best room whenever you visit.
{npc} is relieved and slightly embarrassed.

events.text: {npc} has been accused of theft by the local magistrate, and swears {he} is innocent.

ok.log: You find the stolen silver under the accuser's own floor. {npc} walks free and weeps.

fail.log: You find nothing. {npc} is flogged and released. {He} knows you tried.

effects.log: {npc} is flogged. {He} never mentions it again. Neither do you.

mem.note: did not help when I was accused

events.text: {npc} cannot read or write and asks you to write a letter home to {his} mother.

effects.log: {He} dictates slowly. It is full of love and bad spelling that you do not correct.

mem.note: wrote to my mother for me

effects.log: It takes a year. The first letter {he} writes alone is to thank you.

events.text: {npc} has a duel at dawn and needs a second to stand with {him}.

effects.log: You stand behind {npc} in the cold. {He} wins, barely, and does not let go of your arm afterwards.
It takes all night. At dawn {npc} does not go. {He} is alive, and not sure {he} forgives you.

events.text: {npc}'s child is sick and needs a herb that only grows by the old shrine on the mountain.

ok.log: You come back scratched and triumphant. The child recovers in a week.

fail.log: You fall and hurt your leg, but you bring the herb. The child lives.

effects.log: The herb arrives two days later than it might have. It is enough.

events.text: {npc}'s younger brother has run off to join the bandits in the hills.

ok.log: You find the boy cold and hungry and ready to come home. {npc} cannot speak for joy.

fail.log: The boy will not come. You leave him a coat and a message. He comes home in spring.

effects.log: {npc} is furious. The boy returns in a year, older and quieter.

events.text: {npc} has hurt {his} back and the harvest is waiting.

effects.log: Two weeks of hard labour. {npc} watches from the doorway, proud and annoyed.
The harvest comes in. {npc} complains about the cost for a year.

variants: {npc} has wrenched {his} back, and the harvest will not wait.

events.text: {npc} quietly admits the family owes money to a lender who has started sending men round.

effects.log: You pay. The men stop coming. {npc} cannot look you in the eye for a week, then hugs you.

choices.text: Have a word with the lender

ok.log: The lender forgives half and apologises for the rest.

fail.log: The lender's men are better than they looked. You pay anyway, bruised.

variants: {npc} admits, very quietly, that the family owes a moneylender, and the lender has begun sending men to the door.

events.text: {npc} wants to visit an old friend in a far-off town one last time, but is afraid of the road.

effects.log: Ten days on the road together. The reunion makes both old people cry. So do you, a little.

mem.note: took me to see my old friend

effects.log: {npc} goes in comfort and comes back with presents for you.

events.text: {npc} catches your sleeve in a crowded inn. 'Do not eat the fish tonight,' {he} whispers. 'You {debt}. Now we are even.'

effects.log: You eat rice. Two merchants at the next table are carried out at midnight. {npc} is gone.
{npc} shakes {his} head. 'Better you do not.' {He} pays for your meal and leaves.

events.text: {npc} has become somebody. 'You {debt},' {he} says, 'so let me introduce you to people who matter.'

effects.log: A season of dinners with sect elders and rich merchants. Doors open that were shut.
{npc} insists on paying for your tea for the rest of your life, which is almost as good.

variants: {npc} is someone important now. 'You {debt},' {he} says, 'so let me introduce you to the people who count.'

events.text: {npc} arrives with a long cloth bundle. 'You {debt}. I have waited a long time to give you this.'

effects.log: A fine blade, made for your hand. {npc} had a smith measure you from memory.

choices.text: Tell {him} there was never a debt

effects.log: {npc} refuses to take it back and leaves it at your door. You keep it.

variants: {npc} arrives carrying something long wrapped in cloth. 'You {debt}. I have waited years to give you this.'

events.text: Bandits corner you on a narrow road, and {npc} rides out of nowhere, sword drawn. 'You {debt}!' {he} shouts. 'Now we are even!'

effects.log: Together you drive them off. Afterwards you sit on the road and laugh like fools.
{npc} handles it. You are impressed. {He} is very pleased about that.

events.text: {npc} has spent years perfecting one technique, and wants to teach it to you because you {debt_of}.

effects.log: A month of hard training under a grateful teacher. Your arts leap forward.

choices.text: Learn it, and teach {him} something back

effects.log: It becomes a trade, then a friendship.

variants: {npc} has spent years polishing a single technique, and now wants to pass it to you, because you {debt_of}.

events.text: {npc} pulls you aside. 'You {debt}. So here is something worth more than silver: a hidden cache in the old watchtower.'

ok.log: Under the loose stone: a pouch of silver. {npc} was right.

fail.log: Someone got there first. Only an empty box and a note: 'Too slow.'

effects.log: 'You are strange,' {npc} says, and then, 'thank you.'

events.text: {npc} gives you something wrapped in red cloth. 'For everything. You {debt}.'

effects.log: The family's old jade pendant, the one you were never allowed to touch as a child.
'Take it,' {npc} says, 'or I will be angry until I die.' You take it.

variants: {npc} presses a small packet in red cloth into your hands. 'For all of it. You {debt}.'

events.text: It starts raining and {npc} holds an umbrella over you without a word, getting soaked {him}self.

effects.log: You walk very close together. Neither of you mentions how slowly you walk.
You arrive soaked and happy. The coat comes back three days later, smelling of flowers.

events.text: {npc} asks, very casually, whether you are going to the lantern festival. {He} is not casual at all.

effects.log: You float one lantern between you. What you each wish for, neither says.

mem.note: went to the festival with me

effects.log: {npc} smiles too brightly. You see {him} at the festival alone, watching the lanterns.

events.text: You find a small carved figure on your doorstep. It looks a lot like you. {npc} is very obviously not looking at your house.

effects.log: {npc} goes red to the ears. You talk until the sun goes down.
A silent exchange of gifts begins, and lasts all year.

mem.note: answered my gift with a gift

events.text: You come back from a fight bleeding, and {npc} is waiting with bandages and a furious face.

effects.log: {He} scolds you the whole time {he} binds your wounds. {His} hands are shaking.
'You always say that,' {npc} says, and holds your hand a little too long.

events.text: {npc} leaves a poem in your book. It is about someone with your eyes and your terrible temper.

effects.log: Your poem is worse. {npc} keeps it for the rest of {his} life.
'Nobody,' says {npc}, very quickly. You both know.

events.text: {npc} slams a cup down in front of you in the teahouse. 'You {grudge}. Outside. Now.'

ok.log: It is short. {npc} ends up in the horse trough. The whole teahouse applauds.

fail.log: {npc} beats you in front of everyone. You pay for your own tea, bruised.

ok.log: By the third cup {npc} is complaining about {his} life instead. The grudge softens.

fail.log: {npc} throws the cup. You duck. You leave.

events.text: A figure lands on the roof tiles above your window at night: {npc}, now {npc_realm}. 'For what you {grudge}. Come up.'

ok.log: Tiles fly. At the end {npc} slides off the roof into a pile of hay. The neighbours cheer.

fail.log: You fall through someone's roof into their dinner. {npc} is gone.

effects.log: {npc} shouts insults until dawn. The whole street hates you both now.

events.text: The whole town is whispering about you and a married merchant. It is completely untrue. It started with {npc}.

ok.log: You make the whole square laugh at the story, and at {npc}. It dies.

fail.log: The more you deny it, the more people believe it.

effects.log: The merchant's wife glares at you for a year. Then it fades.

events.text: People say you ran from a fight and let a friend die. The story is always told by {npc}.

choices.text: Dare {npc} to repeat it to your face

ok.log: {npc} will not. That is answer enough for everyone.

fail.log: {npc} repeats it, and beats you when you swing. The rumour grows.

effects.log: It takes years. It works.

events.text: The cook at your usual inn quietly says a customer asked which dish is yours. The description sounds like {npc}.

choices.text: Eat somewhere else for a while

effects.log: You change inns. The cook later tells you someone poured something into your bowl that night.

ok.log: You swap bowls and watch. {npc} flees when you stand up. Everyone saw.

fail.log: Nobody comes. The waiting frightens you more than any fight.

events.text: A drunk mercenary brags that someone paid him well to break your legs. He mentions {npc}'s name.

choices.text: Pay him double to forget it

effects.log: He takes the money, laughs and leaves town.

choices.text: Travel only by day for a while

effects.log: You change your habits. Nothing happens. You never know if something would have.

events.text: On a rope bridge over a gorge, two figures step out at each end. One of them is {npc}.

ok.npcDie: the gorge below the rope bridge
ok.log: The bridge sways, a body falls. When it stops swaying, {npc} is gone into the gorge.

fail.deathCause: a fall from the rope bridge
fail.log: You go over the ropes into the river far below and wake on a sandbank a day later.

choices.text: Cut the ropes and jump for the rocks

ok.log: You land on a ledge. They land in the river. {npc} will hate you even more now.

fail.log: You land badly. You crawl out, but alive.

events.text: You wake at night in an inn to the smell of smoke under your door, and {npc}'s voice outside giving orders.

ok.log: You drop into the yard and are gone before they reach your room. The inn burns. {npc} thinks you died.

fail.log: You fall into the yard among them, and fight your way out.

choices.text: Kick down the door and fight

ok.log: You come out of the smoke like a demon. {npc} does not get away.

fail.log: The smoke is on their side. You barely escape.

events.text: The sect's ledger shows silver missing, and the handwriting on the forged page is {npc}'s. Now the elders say you took it.

ok.log: You match the handwriting in front of the elders. {npc} is expelled. {He} swears revenge.

fail.log: The elders do not believe you. You are fined and shamed.

effects.log: {npc} laughs. 'Prove it.' You cannot, yet.

events.text: {npc} has torn a sleeve again, and you are mending it by the lamp, the way {he} used to watch you do when {he} was small.

effects.log: {npc} says nothing for an hour, then says everything. It is one of the best evenings of the year.
Your patience runs thin by the second stitch, and holds. {npc}'s stitches are awful and getting better.
